title: Short Stuff: Uncle Sam Wants YOU!
summary: Short Stuff episode on Uncle Sam, the personification of the United States. The hosts describe the familiar image (top hat, goatee, flag suit, pointing "I want you" poster) and credit James Montgomery Flagg's 1917 WWI recruitment poster, which was inspired by a Lord Kitchener poster and used Flagg's own face as the model and was printed about four million times. They explain the popular story that Uncle Sam originated with meatpacker Sam Wilson's stamped beef barrels in the War of 1812, and note historians Don Hickey and Christopher Philippo found an 1810 diary entry by a sixteen-year-old sailor on the USS Wasp using the term, predating the story. They discuss the earlier personification Brother Jonathan, the transition to Thomas Nast's imagery, Uncle Sam in political cartoons, and tangents about a 1996 slasher film called Uncle Sam and actor Robert Forster, Breaking Bad, and Quentin Tarantino.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter about where they previously discussed Uncle Sam, guessing a Fourth of July special, and announce the topic.

segments.title: Describing Uncle Sam's look
segments.summary: The hosts describe Uncle Sam's iconic look, including the red, white and blue top hat, flag suit and goatee, and the pointing 'I Want You' poster. They mention a Simpsons immigration episode that parodied the poster.

segments.title: James Montgomery Flagg and WWI posters
segments.summary: James Montgomery Flagg's 1917 WWI poster, which used his own face as the model and was reportedly inspired by a Lord Kitchener poster, was printed about four million times. The hosts note Uncle Sam existed for about a century before this poster.

segments.title: Sam Wilson origin story
segments.summary: The popular story says Uncle Sam came from Sam Wilson, a New York meatpacker whose stamped beef barrels for the War of 1812 were called Uncle Sam's, leading to a 1961 congressional resolution. The hosts say this story is not the true origin.

segments.title: 1810 diary evidence
segments.summary: Historians Don Hickey and Christopher Philippo found an 1810 diary entry by a 16-year-old sailor on the USS Wasp referring to Uncle Sam, showing the term predated the Sam Wilson story. The hosts discuss how Wilson likely helped popularize it.

segments.title: Brother Jonathan and Thomas Nast
segments.summary: Brother Jonathan was an earlier personification of America from around the Revolution, handing off to Uncle Sam as America matured. Thomas Nast helped shape the more modern image, which Flagg then made iconic.

segments.title: Uncle Sam in political cartoons
segments.summary: The hosts note Uncle Sam continues to appear in political cartoons, adapted to whatever message the cartoonist wants.

segments.title: Uncle Sam slasher film and tangents
segments.summary: The hosts mention a 1996 slasher film called Uncle Sam with Robert Forster, discuss his role on Breaking Bad, and digress into Quentin Tarantino and Jackie Brown.

segments.title: Sign-off and ad
segments.summary: The hosts close the Short Stuff and an iHeartRadio production credit is read.
